outcome: admission to Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU)
cohort: The study included 66 low-risk singleton pregnancies with isolated oligohydramnios (AFI <5 cm) and 132 low-risk singleton pregnancies with normal AFI (5-24 cm), all between 34 and 40 weeks of gestation.
finding: Isolated oligohydramnios is associated with higher rates of labour induction, caesarean delivery, and low birth weight, with adverse neonatal outcomes potentially attributed to prematurity and low birth weight rather than isolated oligohydramnios itself.
mod_finding: Isolated oligohydramnios was associated with significantly higher rates of labour induction and caesarean delivery.
